documents.title: Urogynecology Consultation
documents.author: urogynecology
documents.body:
Outside urogynecology practice
Visit date: 01/06/2023
Patient: Aisha Pierre, 43 y/o
Referred by: her gynecologist; copy to primary care

HPI: Seen by gynecology in July and October for leakage. She reports that losing urine with coughing and exercise has steadily progressed over roughly the last six months in spite of pelvic floor exercises. Menses are regular. No hot flashes or other menopausal symptoms.

OB history: four term vaginal deliveries, the last with a prolonged second stage; one first-trimester miscarriage treated with D&C.
Other history: generalized anxiety disorder; fibroid uterus on ultrasound in October.
Medications: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal fibroids.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, marketing consultant.

Vitals: weight 70.8 kg, height 165 cm, BMI 26.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no masses felt.
Cough stress test with a comfortably full bladder: positive, with leakage synchronous with cough.
Urinalysis: negative.

Assessment: stress urinary incontinence, confirmed on exam.

Recommendations:
1. Continue daily pelvic floor muscle training. Reviewed technique; she is isolating the right muscles.
2. Return to this clinic as needed if she would like to discuss further options.

Allergies: NKDA.

Urogynecology

documents.title: Urogyn note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Aisha, I got the urogynecology note from last week. They confirmed stress incontinence and want you to keep up the pelvic floor exercises for now, and you can go back to them whenever you want to talk about other options. Let me know if you have questions.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis compared with 2022 and 2021. Heterogeneously dense breasts. No suspicious masses, calcifications or areas of distortion.

documents.title: Mammogram
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Aisha, your mammogram from yesterday was normal. No follow-up needed until next year.

documents.title: Scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to move her fall physical from 10/4 to later in the month due to a client trip. Rebooked 10/18 at 8:30. Fasting reminder given.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 43F.

Interval: saw urogyn in January, positive cough stress test, confirmed SUI. Plan was to keep doing the exercises. She has been fairly faithful, leakage is "livable", still wears a liner on workout days. Not ready to talk about anything more.
Fibroids: periods still heavy the first couple days, no worse. No lightheadedness.
Anxiety: GAD-7 7. Steady. The walking group helps.

Meds: prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Weight about where it was. Throat clear. Thyroid smooth, normal size. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext no edema. Skin normal. Calm, organized.

Plan
- Routine labs.
- Flu + updated covid today.
- Mammogram order for winter.
- Pap/HPV due next year.
- See you next October.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of your labs came back normal, Aisha, including the blood count. Same plan as before.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 2023, 2022 and 2021. Heterogeneously dense parenchyma, unchanged. No suspicious finding.

documents.title: Check in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, can I come in sometime in April just to talk about stress? Work has been a lot since January and I've been waking up at 3am running through lists. Not an emergency.

documents.title: RE: Check in
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Of course. You are booked Wednesday 4/10 at 1:40 with your doctor. Reply here if that time doesn't work.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Aisha, we missed you yesterday afternoon. Do you want to reschedule? You can also text the office line and we can set up a video visit if that is easier.

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So sorry, client call ran over and I completely forgot. Things have calmed down since the big project wrapped up last week. I'm OK to wait until my physical, I'll reach out if it ramps up again.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical cytology. Specimen adequate; transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

orders.reason: Average-risk colorectal cancer screening, starting at 45

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, 44F, turns 45 next month.

Spring was rough with work (missed her April visit). Better since then but the baseline worry is a notch higher this year, GAD-7 9. Sleeping OK now. We talked about meds and therapy again; she'd rather keep using what works for her and check back in. Fair.
SUI: unchanged, manages with liners and the exercises.
Fibroids: heavy first two days, unchanged.
No GI issues.

Meds: prenatal vitamin. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Ears and throat fine. Neck without nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap and HPV collected. Bimanual: uterus enlarged and irregular, as known; no adnexal fullness. No edema.

Plan
- Pap with HPV collected.
- Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids.
- Colon screening: she turns 45 in November; prefers the stool test. FIT kit given, do after her birthday.
- Flu and covid today.
- Mammogram is on an every-other-year schedule now, next early 2026.
- GAD: monitor; reach out anytime.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from Wednesday are all normal. Pap result will take another few days.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap smear is normal and the HPV test is negative. With both normal, the next one isn't due for five years.
